etsyFees.$comment: Etsy seller fee model used by the per-variant price floor and package-report. Payment processing (4% + EUR 0.30, Ireland) and the 6.5% transaction fee are owner-confirmed from Etsy's help page (checked 2026-10-15). The listing fee (USD 0.20) and the fee rates were confirmed from the Etsy shop setup fee screen on 2026-10-15. Transaction fee applies to the total excluding tax; processing fee to the total including tax and postage (estimated sales tax line, default 0%). The VAT rate on the processing fee is the Irish standard rate and is STILL UNCONFIRMED against an Etsy statement. Offsite Ads (15%) is a worst-case column only, never in the default or the floor. Shipping is modelled per config.shippingPolicy (fees apply to item price + shipping charged); currency conversion is NOT modelled. UPDATED 2026-10-16: VAT now applies to ALL three seller fees (vatOnSellerFees, default on, 23%, unconfirmed: check the first Etsy statement); see digitalProducts for the VAT rule on future digital items.

sloganScoring.$comment: OWNER SETS (2026-10-15, raised 2026-10-16). QA DESIGN scores EVERY option 1-5 for clarity (readable in under 2 seconds, joke lands on first read), audienceFit (about the brief's audience), originality (not a stock tee pun or template) and cleverness (actually funny or clever: a twist, reversal or pun, not just a description of the situation). Average per option. The gate refuses an approval unless the BEST option averages at least minAverage AND the CHOSEN option averages at least minAverage with no dimension below minEach and every dimension in minByDimension at or above its figure. A slogan that only describes the situation scores cleverness 1-2 and fails. When the owner has picked the slogan (ownerPick in the slogan record) the owner's pick stands: the chosen-option thresholds are not applied, but every option must still be scored.

sloganScreen.$comment: LOCAL BLOCKLIST ONLY, owner-maintained (2026-10-15): brands, sports teams and leagues, famous catchphrases, characters. A hit blocks QA approval and packaging. A clear result is NOT trademark clearance: every text-led listing carries the owner to-do 'check slogan on USPTO trademark search before publishing'. Matching is on whole words after lower-casing and removing punctuation. Add to the lists as you find more; never remove without the owner. The 'saturated' list is a SEED of stock tee slogans and templates (owner: reject common existing slogans as unoriginal and flag possible trademark risk); it is local, non-exhaustive and not trademark clearance. QA DESIGN also judges saturation from its own knowledge. EXTENDED 2026-10-16 (originality gate): lists people, franchises, lyrics-and-quotes, artists, derivative. These are SEEDS of well-known protected names and phrases, local and non-exhaustive: a clear result is never clearance, and QA DESIGN / QA LISTING still judge anything the lists cannot know. Matching also catches case, punctuation, accents, plurals and possessives, spaced-out letters (n i k e), compounds (spiderman), digit/symbol swaps (n1ke) and single-letter misspellings of long names (addidas). Every category except saturated hard-fails QA DESIGN, QA LISTING and the package gate; saturated applies to slogans only.

nearMissAllow.$comment: OWNER exception to the station freeze (2026-10-17): ordinary words that must NOT count as a one-letter misspelling of the listed name. Applies only to the near-miss-spelling match; the name itself (and its plural, compound or symbol-swap forms) still hits. Keys are listed phrases, values are the ordinary words. Exact whole words only (after case and punctuation): no plural stripping, no fuzzy match, so list every form (owner, 2026-10-17). Add only with the owner.

phraseAllow.$comment: OWNER-APPROVED exact phrases (owner, 2026-10-18, DECISIONS.md "E6 wrap-up"): a listed phrase does not hit where it is part of one of these phrases, word for word. Exact phrase only, after case and punctuation: no plural or possessive forms, no compound or misspelling; the listed phrase alone, or in any other phrase, still hits ("apple" stays blocked). Add only with the owner.

cleanup.enclosedNote: owner exception 2026-10-16 (the mug's handle hole was opaque off-white): first, an ENCLOSED region of opaque (alpha >= 128), light (luminance >= minLum) and nearly grey (max - min channel <= maxChroma) pixels, solid (>= minRegionPx, average width >= minWidthPx) with no clear pixel or image edge within ringPx, whose ring is at least minOutlineShare outline-dark (luminance <= outlineMaxLum), is made transparent; its anti-aliased edge within fringePx is unmixed into the outline colour. Calibrated on the mug: hole RGB 254,249,237 (luminance 249, chroma 17), body 255,237,193 (237, 62), steam fill 255,242,210 (chroma 45). The finished file is re-checked with the same colour and size thresholds at any outline share; the package gate refuses a file with one left. A genuinely white, outlined part (paper, eye whites) would also be cleared: the review images show it.
cleanup.paletteNote: owner rule 2026-10-17 for the products listed: no pure-white or grey-white fills; paper, book pages, sticky notes and eye highlights use cream or pale palette tints, each fill's colour channels differing by more than maxChroma (the clean-up's 24). The build records, per file: (1) every pixel opaque in the generated file that the enclosed step made fully clear, and how many of them were NOT background-coloured there (background-coloured = luminance >= backgroundMinLum and channels within maxChroma; the generated file stores no background colour of its own, its clear pixels are black, so the removed pixels' own colour is the test); (2) near-white fills of the cleaned artwork: solid regions (>= minRegionPx, average width >= minWidthPx, at the generator's size) of opaque pixels with luminance >= nearWhiteMinLum and channels within maxChroma. The package gate fails (1) for every packaged product and (2) for the products listed. nearWhiteMinLum 200 is Claude's choice for 'grey-white', not an owner figure. Limit: a pure-white outlined fill drawn against the rule is cleared like a hole and passes (1); the review images and QA DESIGN (the brief's Quality bar) catch it.
cleanup.note: at the generator's size: alpha below alphaFloor -> fully clear (faint haze and fringe); alpha at or above alphaSolid -> fully solid; separate opaque specks of speckMaxPx pixels or fewer removed; colour under fully clear pixels zeroed; then trimmed to the artwork. alphaFloor is applied again after the upscale (resampling leaves faint ringing).

build.paddingNote: every prop is centred on its square canvas with its longer side filling 100 - 2 x paddingPct per cent (6 = 120 px each side at 2000 px), so all files in a pack sit the same way

optimise.$comment: OWNER exception to the station freeze (2026-10-17): the 12-file prop pack zipped at 28.1-28.3 MB, over Etsy's 20 MB per file. Every finished PNG is first re-encoded LOSSLESSLY (zlib level 9 with adaptive row filtering: the same pixels, checked). If the zip is then still over paletteIfZipOverBytes, every file is palette-reduced with libimagequant (the engine pngquant uses, built into sharp) at quality 100 with Floyd-Steinberg dithering, and the zip re-checked. sharp has no pngquant-style minimum quality, so a file whose palette version is below minPsnrDb (premultiplied RGBA PSNR against the lossless file) keeps the lossless version and a warning is recorded. Pixel size is never changed (2000x2000). The gate measures the real zip on disk.
